speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand what might be causing this, have you noticed any family members with similar bleeding problems, and are you currently taking any aspirin or other blood thinning medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP)

Since the bleeding symptoms are localized to the mucous membranes and extremities without the severe organomegaly or abnormal bleeding pattern seen in platelet function disorders, I will now request a Complete Blood Count (CBC) with peripheral smear to confirm the platelet count.
